Jonas/ Lauren — draft benchmark details below (notes from local run on dedicated 1xA100 equivalent instance):

Test harness (short):
- runner: k6-based harness with 64 worker threads, open-loop driver to impose a constant RPS profile.
- RTT shaping: 30ms client RTT added to emulate east-coast traffic.
- concurrency: tests run at target in-flight requests of [1, 8, 32, 128] to show scaling shape.
- warm vs cold: warm = after 60s of continuous requests (KV cache populated); cold = first request after >10 minutes idle.
- model: redwood-7b-repro (int8-quantized path) used for baseline.
- batch settings: continuous batching ON, batching window 20ms, max batch size 12.

Observed summary (single-GPU, seq = prompt(128) + gen(128) => total 256 tokens):
- p50 latency (request wall-time): 2.3s at concurrency=1, 0.58s per 64 tokens equivalent when normalized to steady-state per-token.
- p95 latency: 3.9s at concurrency=1. Under concurrency=32, p95 increases to ~5.6s (queuing + batch formation effects).
- sustained throughput: with concurrency=32 and continuous batching, sustained throughput measured as ~18k tokens/sec (aggregate).
- peak observed short-window throughput (burst): ~27k tokens/sec for 30s windows with larger batching.

Scaling behavior notes:
- linear-ish throughput scaling from 1 → 4 GPUs for this model for throughput-oriented tests; per-request latency increases sublinearly with load because batches amortize kernel cost.
- if KV caching is applicable (multi-turn), effective per-token latency improves ~25–35% due to avoided recomputation.
- quantization: int8 path used here gives ~1.6× tokens/sec improvement vs fp16 at similar p95 latency.

Attachments for the client: redwood_benchmark_snapshot_v1.pdf (tables + graphs), redwood_test_harness_instructions.md (how to reproduce), small snippets of k6 scripts.

I can convert numbers into a concise table for client-facing doc.

-rishi

Emma — thank you for the questionnaire and the probe results. Attached is a short methodology note and our benchmark snapshot (PDF). Below is a concise summary that maps directly to the fields in your spreadsheet.

Summary (mapping to your rows):
- Test harness: k6-based open-loop driver, 64 workers, RTT shaping 30ms applied (we included the harness README).
- Warm vs cold: warm = after 60s of continuous requests (server-side KV cache primed). Cold = first request after >10 minutes idle. We provide both warm and cold numbers in the attached PDF.
- Model & quantization: redwood-7b-repro, int8 optimized path (quantized kernels) used for the snapshot.
- p50/p95 (seq=128→gen=128, single-GPU dedicated run): p50 = 2.3s, p95 = 3.9s (wall-clock request time).
- Sustained throughput: measured over a 10-minute steady-state window at concurrency=32. Sustained aggregate throughput = ~18k tokens/sec. Peak short-window bursts (30s) reached ~27k tokens/sec.
- Scaling: throughput scales near-linearly up to 4 GPUs for this model; recommend a shared pool (2–4 GPUs) for production load bursts.
- Repro artifacts: attached redwood_test_harness_instructions.md with k6 snippet and the CSV we used for the runs.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_snapshot_v1.pdf, redwood_test_harness_instructions.md

If you want us to run the harness using your exact probe CSV and provide a side-by-side comparison (same RTT shaping and concurrency), we can do that under a short NDA or via a dedicated test endpoint.
